title: TypeError: FabricDeepSpeedZeroOptimizer is not an Optimizer
body:
### Bug description

In the scenario where fabric uses deepspeed stragety, lr_scheduler will make an error 
TypeError: FabricDeepSpeedZeroOptimizer is not an Optimizer

### What version are you seeing the problem on?

master

### How to reproduce the bug

```python
213 def load_lr_scheduler(optimizer, num_step):
214     args.overrode_max_train_steps = False
215     args.num_update_steps_per_epoch = math.ceil(num_step / args.gradient_accumulation_steps)
216     if args.max_train_steps is None:
217         args.max_train_steps = args.num_train_epochs * args.num_update_steps_per_epoch
218         args.overrode_max_train_steps = True
219 
220     lr_scheduler = get_scheduler(
221         name=args.lr_scheduler_type,
222         optimizer=optimizer,
223         num_warmup_steps=args.num_warmup_steps * args.gradient_accumulation_steps,
224         num_training_steps=args.max_train_steps * args.gradient_accumulation_steps,
225     )
226     return lr_scheduler
...
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
This is because the DeepSpeedOptimizer from the deepspeed library itself is not of type `torch.optim.Optimizer` either. And so, when Fabric warps it, then naturally the instance check fails with that wrapper class too. See [here](https://github.com/microsoft/DeepSpeed/blob/4e886f0568832d292183926bcc1a9105def25f2c/deepspeed/runtime/__init__.py#L11) in deepspeed, their optimizers just inherit from this class. It's just a plain class that has nothing to do with torch Optimizer.



For optimizers that are subclasses of `torch.optim.Optimizer`, our wrapper will pass the instance check. For example, here we test this:

https://github.com/Lightning-AI/lightning/blob/a36af3f9f855a4735fdc97c5e08bebb8a7467bf3/tests/tests_fabric/test_wrappers.py#L293-L299

@participant5 Honestly I'm not sure what Lightning can do here. Suggestions welcome.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Closing this as https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/issues/17584#issuecomment-1537258527 seems to be the only solution. Anything set up with Fabric requires PyTorch optimizers. If someone still has issues with this, please also open a ticket on the DeepSpeed repo about the `DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer` not being a Optimizer subclass.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I once added support for "Optimizables" as optimizers to the Trainer: https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/pull/16189

Couldn't Fabric do the same? This requires that the deepspeed optimizer follows the same methods and API, even if it doesn't subclass the torch optimizer

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @participant3 The error happens in `lr_scheduler = load_lr_scheduler(optimizer, len(train_dataloader))` which is in user code not in Fabric. After the optimizer is set up by the strategy, it is what it is. In case of DeepSpeed, it is just their special class. Which is why I suggest defining the scheduler before setup.
